What Plumline can do

Plumline turns a spreadsheet-shaped model into an optimised decision, then checks the result against your own formulas. Here is what it can model, how it verifies each answer, and what it explains — with a runnable example wherever one applies.

Models Spreadsheet support Verification Explanation & visualisation

Models

Continuous models

Split resources in any proportion to hit the best objective.

Limit: Linear relationships only — non-linear formulas are rejected, not approximated.

Open this example in the solver

Integer models

Whole-number decisions, like units produced or people assigned.

Limit: Larger integer models take longer to prove optimal.

Open this example in the solver

Binary decisions

Yes/no choices: pick a project, open a site, ship an order.

Open this example in the solver

Mixed-integer models

Combine continuous and whole-number decisions in one model.

Open this example in the solver

Maximise or minimise

Aim for the most profit or the least cost; confirm the direction yourself.

Open this example in the solver

Spreadsheet support

Number or formula limits

A constraint limit can be a number or a formula from your sheet.

Open this example in the solver

Paste from a spreadsheet

Paste a range from Excel or Google Sheets, or type into the grid.

Export results

Download results as CSV or Excel, or copy a plain-text summary.

Verification

Objective re-checked

The reported objective is recomputed from your formulas at the solution.

Open this example in the solver

Constraints re-checked

Every constraint is re-checked against the solved values.

Open this example in the solver

Runs in your browser

Solving happens in your browser; the model is not uploaded to a server.

Explanation & visualisation

Shows what it understood

Reads the objective, decisions and constraints and shows them before solving.

Open this example in the solver

Marginal impact

Estimates how much a binding limit would improve the objective if relaxed by one unit.

Limit: Estimated only for eligible binding constraints in continuous models.

Open this example in the solver

Feasible-region chart

Draws the feasible region for two-variable models, bounded or unbounded.

Limit: Available for two-variable models, within a practical numeric range.

Open this example in the solver

Five languages

Interface and explanations in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German and French.

Errors in your language

Engine messages appear in the active language on every screen.

Try it on a real model

Open an example in the solver, or paste your own spreadsheet model and see it interpreted, solved and checked.
